title: NBA won’t punish Bam Adebayo for punching Tyler Herro in Las Vegas
content:
The NBA will not punish Miami Heat star Bam Adebayo for punching former teammate Tyler Herro at a Las Vegas hotel and gym last week, a league spokesperson told The Athletic.

“After discussing with the players involved and the NBPA, everyone would prefer to move on from this unfortunate circumstance, and no further action will be taken by the league,” the spokesperson said.

The Milwaukee Bucks, the Heat and the NBPA declined to comment.

On Friday, Herro’s AAU team was practicing inside Resorts World Las Vegas hotel. Herro appeared to yell something at Adebayo, who made his way toward Herro and then threw a punch. Players and coaches quickly broke up the altercation, and Adebayo made his way out of the hotel.

Adebayo and Herro were teammates for seven years in Miami before Herro was traded to Milwaukee as part of the package of players and picks the Bucks received to move two-time NBA MVP Giannis Antetokounmpo.

Following the trade, a fan leaked a series of screenshots of direct messages that appeared to come from an Instagram account connected to Herro. In those alleged direct messages, Herro appeared to question Adebayo’s game and whether he was worthy of the contracts he has signed with the Heat.

It is not uncommon for the NBA to leave discipline for altercations that occur outside of league games or league-sponsored events to the teams or other organizations involved, rather than issue its own punishment.

In 2017, Bobby Portis punched Nikola Mirotić during a Chicago Bulls practice, leaving Mirotić with facial fractures and a concussion. The Bulls, not the NBA, suspended Portis for eight games.

In October 2022, Draymond Green punched then-Warriors teammate Jordan Poole during a Golden State practice. Green spent several days away from the team following the incident, but the NBA did not suspend him. The Warriors handled the discipline themselves, fining Green an undisclosed amount but ultimately deciding not to suspend him.

There is also precedent involving Charles Barkley and Charles Oakley. During the NBA lockout in 1998, Oakley slapped Barkley during a players’ union meeting — an event not conducted by the NBA — and the league did not discipline either player for the altercation. The two had previously fought during an NBA preseason game in 1996, an incident for which both players were suspended and fined by the league.
